decisions.summary: joined_link: the straight snap where walkable, else the clear run of it the far-gap branch lays (clear_runs), else the run is refused; used by the end branch and to carry a cut end onto the way
decisions.why: This is row 486's ranked fix for the end branch, word for word: 'when _clear_link fails, lays a routed link as the far-gap branch does (clear_runs) or refuses the run'. It meets wave 43 round 2's condition that the routed link is tried before the refusal, for the end branch and the cut end. A fragment that stops up to 12 ft short of the network is closed by the later touch pass (touch.py join reach, 25 ft), so it is not a gap that 0081 forbids.

decisions.summary: A run kept whole (both halves 40 ft or more) has its arriving vertex run[k] snapped onto its foot. It is refused where joined_link(run[k], q) is None, or where either new leg run[k-1]->q or q->run[k+1] is not walkable
decisions.why: The snap itself is the ranked fix ('the mid-run branch snaps run[k] to its foot'). The two refusals around it are carve-outs, and neither rests on impossibility. (a) The gate on joined_link refuses on the walkability of p->q, but the snap removes p, and the two new legs are tested on their own. A run whose legs are clear is refused because of an obstacle that no drawn ink would touch. (b) Where the legs are blocked but joined_link HAS found a walkable link, the run is refused. Yet the far-gap branch's own mechanism draws exactly that link as its own lane (_draw_web(s, link[0], w), then the run). Wave 43 round 2 set the condition that the refusal owes the routed link first, so that a run is not drawn only where NO link is walkable. The dispatch says these are the conditions that round set. They are not: round 2 did not prescribe a refusal on the snapped legs. Fix: snap where both new legs are walkable. Otherwise, where joined_link returns a link, draw it as its own lane joining run[k] to the network, as the far-gap branch does. Refuse only where neither exists. Then restate the claim at serve.py:134 ('or not drawn where that link is not walkable', unchanged by this wave, though round 2 required it) to say 'not drawn where no link is walkable', and cover the snap of a run kept whole. Add a test for each of the three outcomes, red on the current code.

decisions.summary: law.reach_to_steading: 0246's 60 ft measured to the house's CENTER, the 12 ft to the built ground including the house's own footprint
decisions.why: 0246.drawing's note at the rule says 'WAY_END_REACH_FT 60 (to a way's line or a farmhouse's center), STEADING_ARRIVAL_FT 12 (to the steading's built ground)'. The bullet lists 'its house' among the built ground at 12 ft. A 60 ft footprint reading would make that clause redundant, and consts.py:276-281 records why the center was chosen. So the center is the page's own measure, and wave 43's footprint reading (which I ruled a plain reading) is correctly withdrawn. The added house-footprint check at STEADING_REACH_FT carries 'its house' from the bullet. Tests: 59 ft from the center reaches, 11 ft off the wall reaches, 75 ft from the center and 60 off the wall does not.

decisions.summary: test_a_house_crowded_with_ends_...: two ends moved from 60.8 and 63.2 ft of the center to 51 ft, so that all three still front the house
decisions.why: The test's premise is three fronting ends and the settle cutting an ordinary one. It is restated under the corrected reach, not weakened: its assertions are unchanged apart from the moved coordinates. The distances were re-derived from the coordinates.

decisions.summary: Wave 43's found row geom.end_serves tiered E3 by a fresh reader and 'left for its place', its fix still 'test 60 ft to the house's footprint edge ... rewrite STEADING_ARRIVAL_FT's rationale, which defends the center measure'
decisions.why: The same wave rules that 0246 measures the 60 ft to the center ('reach-center'), and the plan says 'with the center restored the two now agree on the 60 ft'. So the row's finding (end_serves at centers against reach_to_steading at footprints) no longer holds. Yet it stays ranked DRIFTED with a fix that, executed at its turn, would move end_serves AWAY from the page's own note and undo this wave's correction. A ranked fix that takes a unit off the research narrows 'make the implementation match the research' for that unit. Nothing forces it: the fix is to the record. Fix: close the row in this wave as not drifted, with the reason (both now measure 0246's 60 ft to the center, as the page's note says; end_serves's claims read IN-STEP in dev/claims-index.json), recorded in ranking.json, overrides.json and t113a-out.jsonl's row, or re-read by impl-drift at T114. Do not leave it to be executed as written.
